chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children' - the verse -

He said: O Sulayman, among these weakened ones, there are those with a thicker neck than you. The weakened are a people who fast, pray, whose bellies and private organs are modest; they do not believe that the truth is with other than us, holding onto the branches of the tree. For those, Allah might pardon them if they were to adhere to the branches. Moreover, if they were to not know those, then if Allah was to pardon them, it would be due to His mercy, and if He was to torment them, it would be due to their aberration from what He made them know.

key_terms.آخِذِينَ بِأَغْصَانِ الشَّجَرَةِ: Holding onto the branches of the tree; metaphor for adhering to the truth or the Imams
key_terms.أَثْخَنُ رَقَبَةً: Thicker neck; an idiom for someone more substantial or significant
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفُونَ: The weakened ones; those excused from obligation due to weakness or inability
key_terms.تَعِفُّ بُطُونُهُمْ وَفُرُوجُهُمْ: Their bellies and private organs are modest; referring to fasting and chastity

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the weakened ones' in Surah An-Nisa verse 98 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expands the definition of *al-mustad'afin* beyond physical incapacity to include spiritual resilience, specifically highlighting the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers who maintain chastity and fidelity to the truth despite external constraints. The Imam uses the metaphor of 'holding onto the branches' to signify their adherence to the core tenets of Islam and the Imams, suggesting that their salvation is contingent upon whether they recognized the specific authority of the Imams; if they knew, deviation leads to punishment, but if they did not, mercy prevails. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological emphasis on *taqlid* and the distinction between general obedience and specific recognition of the Imamate.
